title: Logweir chart values
description: Types for every value in values.yaml. The three optional components are switched by booleans and nothing else: `--set demoKafka.enabled=yes` is refused here, before anything renders. Task 38 adds `environment`, `kubernetes`, `imagePullSecrets` and `kafka` — the keys an adopter's own values file needs — and the per-component placement overrides. What this file does NOT type is the `kafka.security` pair and `kafka.secretKey`: those are checked at RENDER time by `templates/_helpers.tpl`, so an unsupported mechanism fails naming the two Logweir speaks rather than as an anonymous schema error.

nodeSelector.description: A node label selector. Empty means no constraint.

secondsOrBuildDefault.description: D3 §2.3/§2.7: an empty string means this controller build's own default and renders no environment variable at all; a whole number of seconds is passed through and clamped up to the build's floor by weirkeeper::diagnostics::bounded. `false` and `no` are refused here so that a YAML boolean can never reach a duration; a NEGATIVE number is refused too, because the one meaningful small value is failFastSeconds: 0 — FAIL_FAST_NEVER — and anything below it is a typo the controller would silently read as the default.

tolerations.description: Pod tolerations, verbatim as Kubernetes spells them.

affinity.description: A pod affinity/anti-affinity block, verbatim as Kubernetes spells it.

visibilityAttestation.description: One administrator completeness attestation (D2 §5.4). EVERY field is required and non-empty: `weirkeeper`'s own `check::policy` refuses an unknown field but would accept a blank `clusterId` or `principal`, and a blank one matches nothing while LOOKING like an attestation an operator can rely on. The two timestamps are RFC 3339. Logweir never verifies the statement; the UI renders `attested by <attestedBy> at <attestedAt>; not verified by Logweir`.

identityLocation.description: One object-store location the controller's OWN identity may read evidence from (D2 §4.4). An unlisted location is refused with `ControllerIdentityNotAllowlisted`, so the empty default is the closed direction.

kafkaCluster.description: One KafkaCluster, in the flat shape an adopter writes. The chart maps `security` onto the CRD's `auth: {mode, tls}` and refuses any combination it cannot speak.

bootstrapServers.description: `host:port,host:port` as the AWS console prints it, or a YAML list. Both are split into the CRD's list.

checks.description: The check-pool ceilings and the two per-kind retention blocks of the installation policy (D2 §4.4), rendered into the `weirkeeper-policy` ConfigMap. Every field is REQUIRED here because `weirkeeper::check::policy` parses the document with `deny_unknown_fields` and no per-field default inside `checks`, `discovery` or `preflight`: a half-written block is a policy the controller refuses at load, and it refuses it fail-closed (no attestations, no allowlist). TWO OF `Policy::validate`'s RULES CANNOT BE WRITTEN HERE, because JSON Schema draft-07 cannot compare two sibling values: `maxActiveTotal >= maxActivePerNamespace` and `discovery.defaultMaxTopics <= discovery.hardMaxTopics`. `templates/policy.yaml` refuses both with a named `fail` at render time, which is the same moment and the same audience.

hardMaxTopics.description: PINNED TO `logweir_core::check_contract::MAX_TOPICS_CEILING`. `Policy::validate` refuses anything above it, and a refused policy fails CLOSED — every attestation and every evidence location is discarded while the install looks healthy — so this bound must equal the constant, never merely resemble it. `weirkeeper::tests::chart_policy::the_schema_bounds_are_the_parsers_own_rules` reads both and fails if they drift.

engine.description: The policy document's `engine` block, and NOT an image: `allowUnverifiedCustomCa` is whether a `BackupDestination` may carry a private CA the archive engine cannot verify. `false` is the closed direction.

notify.description: What the controller tells the delivery Jobs it creates for `ProtectionPolicy` alerts. NOT part of the policy `ConfigMap`: it is rendered as `LOGWEIR_NOTIFY_ALLOW_INSECURE_SINKS` on the `weirkeeper` Deployment, and only when true. `allowInsecureSinks` is the documented local-development escape hatch for a `http://` webhook or Slack URL — `logweir notify deliver` refuses a non-`https://` sink before it dials, so without it an in-cluster echo sink on a laptop cluster receives nothing. It is an INSTALLATION setting and a `ProtectionPolicy` cannot turn it on: a namespaced object that could would let whoever creates a policy downgrade their own alerts' transport to cleartext, carrying the event, the policy's name and (for Slack, where the URL is the credential) a bearer token. Production leaves it `false`.

admissionPolicy.description: The ValidatingAdmissionPolicy that fences the console API ServiceAccount's `create` on Secrets to the two Logweir credential types (D2 §7.3). `enabled` is false by default for ONE reason and it is written down: `admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1` ValidatingAdmissionPolicy is Kubernetes 1.30+ and this chart's floor is 1.29, where the document would be rejected with `no matches for kind`. It is not a security opinion. `consoleServiceAccountName` is REQUIRED and non-empty: the policy's whole effect is its `matchConditions` subject list, and a null or empty name renders a principal string that matches nobody — a fence that installs, reads as enabled, and protects nothing. The template refuses it a second time with `required`, because a values file that omits the key entirely is a different path from one that nulls it.

environment.description: A LABEL — `logweir.dev/environment` on every object this chart renders. It switches nothing else; a key that silently did something would be worse than no key.

kubernetes.description: Node placement for every pod the chart renders, and the one namespace name the chart cannot derive. `namespace` does NOT move the install — `helm -n` / `--namespace` does that, and Release.Namespace is what every object carries; it only supplies `ui.namespaces` when that is empty.

imagePullSecrets.description: Pull secrets, rendered on the controller ServiceAccount, the runner ServiceAccount (so every runner Job inherits them) and every optional component's pods.

controllerImage.description: The weirkeeper image. The default is the repository config/manager/deployment.yaml pins, at the `latest` TAG (the owner's decision of 2026-09-12); `<repository>@sha256:<64 hex>` is accepted and is how you pin it back.

runnerImage.description: The runner image, rendered as LOGWEIR_RUNNER_IMAGE on the Deployment (Task 33). The default is the repository weirkeeper::job::RUNNER_IMAGE pins, at the `latest` TAG.

imagePullPolicy.description: The CONTROLLER container's pull policy. Default `Always`, which is Kubernetes' own default for a `:latest` tag.

runnerImagePullPolicy.description: The RUNNER Jobs' pull policy, rendered as LOGWEIR_RUNNER_PULL_POLICY on the Deployment (Task 37). Default `Always`, because runnerImage names a tag; `Never` for an image you loaded onto the node yourself. The controller refuses to start on anything outside this enum.

watchNamespaces.description: D0 stage 5: the execution namespaces the controller watches and creates Jobs in. Empty is every namespace through the cluster-wide ClusterRoleBinding, the behaviour of every earlier release. A list renders one RoleBinding per namespace instead, a ClusterRole for the two cluster-scoped trust kinds only, and LOGWEIR_WATCH_NAMESPACES on the controller. Shared console mode requires a list that excludes the release namespace, where the console's keys live.

kafka.description: The SOURCE cluster's keys inline, plus `enabled` and an optional `target:` carrying the same keys. `enabled: false` (the default) renders no KafkaCluster at all, which is what every example does today.

retention.description: D3 §9. Renders the `logweir-retention` ServiceAccount the enforcement Job names, and nothing else — no role, because the retention worker makes zero Kubernetes API calls. There is no `image` key: the enforcement binary ships in `runnerImage`.

approvalPolicy.description: PLAT-19.2. The installation's approval policies and namespace bindings (decision D0), rendered once into an immutable, content-addressed ConfigMap mounted into BOTH the weirkeeper controller (LOGWEIR_APPROVAL_POLICY_FILE) and the console (approvalPolicyFile), so both consume the same digest. Empty: every namespace resolves to legacy-governed-v1, today's governed approval. An Ordinary policy is refused unless allowOrdinaryConfirmation is true; a Governed policy always requires a distinct approver principal. A served namespace bound to a policy needs confirmationKeySecret: a Secret with key `confirmation.key`, the console's ConsoleConfirmation PKCS#8 private key, whose public half must be on the namespace's TrustPolicy.

api.description: D3 §9 / PLAT-17.1. `enabled` renders the console/API principal — the ServiceAccount, its two ClusterRoles and one RoleBinding per configured namespace — and starts nothing; `console.enabled` additionally runs the logweir-console image as that principal. Two switches, because D0's rollout has a real state in which the identity exists and is reviewable with `kubectl auth can-i` while no pod runs. `admissionPolicy.consoleServiceAccountName` must name the account `enabled` renders.

console.description: D0 stage 7 calls this block `console.*` and the chart's values call the principal `api.*`; `api.console.*` is both names where a reader needs both. What this file types and what it CANNOT: the schema refuses a non-HTTPS publicBaseUrl, a mode outside the two named ones, a port outside 1-65535 and a session lifetime outside 60-900. It cannot express `shared mode requires oidc.issuer` or `an Ingress requires a TLS secret`, because a JSON Schema conditional there would report an anonymous failure; those are `fail` calls in templates/ui/api-config.yaml, which name the field and say why.

mode.description: THE IN-CLUSTER ADMINISTRATOR MODE (`localAdmin`): a loopback listener with NO Service at all, reached only with `kubectl port-forward deploy/<release>-api` — one configured administrator, no identity provider, no Ingress, the narrowly bound `<release>-api` ServiceAccount, and readiness not gated on OIDC. `shared` is the SSO console and is the ONLY mode that may be exposed through a Service or an Ingress: OIDC, an encrypted session cookie, exact role bindings, and TLS in front. THERE IS NO DEFAULT, here or in the binary — `crates/logweir-api/src/config.rs` refuses a file that forgets to name a mode rather than reading it as the more permissive one, and this chart refuses the same way. The empty string is in this enum only so a values file with the console OFF still validates; `api.console.enabled` with an empty mode is a render-time `fail` naming the field.

publicBaseUrl.description: TLS AT THE SHARED ENTRY POINT IS TYPED HERE, not only checked at render time, so `--set api.console.publicBaseUrl=http://console.example.com` is refused by the schema before a template runs. The pattern also refuses a path, a query, a fragment, userinfo and a trailing slash: the OIDC redirect URI is this value plus /auth/callback, and a value that is wrong here is a login that cannot complete. The empty string is permitted for localAdmin mode, where the field is unused.

requireTrustedProxy.description: Shared mode: refuse (421 misdirected_request) any request, the two probes excepted, whose socket peer is outside trustedProxyCidrs or that the proxy did not mark X-Forwarded-Proto: https. Refused at render time with no CIDR to trust.

clientSecret.description: The NAME of a Secret in the release namespace holding the client secret under the key `clientSecret`. Never the secret itself: a literal here would travel into the rendered manifest, into `helm get manifest`, and into charts/logweir/rendered/.
